scenes.name: Techno-rock y pop de estudio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El «sonido» por encima de la melodía, el ritmo y la armonía: Electric Light Orchestra inventa el «high-tech pop»; Supertramp, Alan Parsons Project, Kansas, Styx y Split Enz. El valor de la producción define a Steely Dan (el pop-jazz pulido de los yuppies), Hall & Oates, los Fleetwood Mac de Rumours y Tusk, Toto, el «muro de sonido» titánico de Jim Steinman (Bat Out Of Hell) y la Penguin Cafe Orchestra. A finales de los setenta, el art-rock culmina en los supergrupos: 10cc, Godley & Creme, Foreigner, UK, Asia, Sky.

podcast.title: Credibility with African-American Musicians/Fans
podcast.body: Despite being white artists, Hall & Oates earned considerable credibility among African-American musicians and fans, a testament to the palpable Philly Soul influences present in their songs like "Sara Smile" and "She's Gone." "Hall and Oates do have credibility with African-American musicians and fans."

podcast.title: Philly Soul Roots Despite New York Move
podcast.body: Even though Hall & Oates declined a contract with Philadelphia International Records and opted to relocate to New York for a different musical direction, their music consistently retained strong "Philly Soul DNA" and roots, demonstrating the lasting impact of their origins. "But the roots are still there."

podcast.title: Premiere Blue-Eyed Soul Act
podcast.body: The duo of Daryl Hall and John Oates achieved significant success by topping both the pop and R&B charts with "I Can't Go For That," becoming recognized as the premiere blue-eyed soul act of their day and demonstrating how artists can confound genre boundaries. "I've chronicled how the duo of Darryl Hall and John Oates became the premiere blue-eyed soul act of their day, topping both the pop and R&B charts with I Can't Go For That."

xref.title: Campaigns for Major Artists
xref.body: During her tenure as an executive, Margo Netts was instrumental in working on marketing and promotional campaigns for a wide array of prominent artists, including Stevie Nicks, Pete Townshend, ABBA, and Hall & Oates. Her influence helped shape the careers of many popular acts. "She worked on campaigns for everyone from Stevie Nicks to Pete Townsend to Abba to Holland Oats."

xref.title: Texas Crime Prevention Center Classified Manson Fans as Gang Members
xref.body: A Texas organization called the Crime Prevention Resource Center classified fans of Marilyn Manson and goth-rock in the same category as gang members, accusing them of drug use, vandalism, and "ritual sacrifices." Recommended responses for schools included locker searches, surveillance of students' books and websites, and psychological hospitalization. The same organization also warned about "evil occultist images" in music by The Beatles and Hall & Oates.
